3F.14 We should hate those that hate God.
Godly Hate

precepts.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. You are asking God to measure you against his word. And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered. Blessed is the man that endures it.
precepts.point: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally. How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No: you have to study, you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you, and as you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, I had not known sin but by the law. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

precepts.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: and see if there be any wicked way in me. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly. And how does he search you? You have to search the scriptures.
precepts.point: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves: not your neighbor. Yourself.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.text: Search me O God and know my heart, try me and know my thoughts, and see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting; God knows your thoughts, so let him try you.
precepts.point: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from secret faults. This should be your reason to be in this walk, not to appear righteous, but because God shall bring every work into judgment; work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.” David prays the same way here: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.”

God knows your thoughts, so let him try you. Ask him to search your heart, to see if there is any wicked way in you, and to lead you in the way everlasting. That is asking to be cleansed from secret faults, the ones you cannot understand yourself.

precepts.text: Every one of us has an angel assigned that beholds the Father's face; one way the Lord sees and knows all things is through the angels who write everything down, though the Lord Himself can see all things at any time He chooses.
precepts.point: At the end he asks the Lord to search him, know his heart, try him, and see if there be any wicked way in him and lead him in the way everlasting.
precepts.why:
“Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Christ says, “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.” Every one of us has an angel assigned that beholds the Father’s face.

One way the Lord sees and knows all things is through the angels, who write everything down, though the Lord himself can see all things at any time he chooses. So when David asks to be searched and tried, he knows nothing is hidden, and the same all-seeing God knows the bloody men who speak against him wickedly, the ones David hates with perfect hatred and counts his enemies.

points: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. Search me, Lord, and know my mind. Because remember the scripture said all evil thoughts start with the mind. Try me means prove me. Prove me, know my thoughts.

And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. So you ask the Most High to try you. Look at my thoughts. See if I have any evil in me. And lead me in the way everlasting. What is that talking about? That is talking about repenting, about changing.

Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts. This is the prayer: Lord, search my heart, try me against your word, and see if there be any wicked way in me. Why does David ask that? Because he knows he cannot serve two masters. Show me, Lord, where I'm falling short, and lead me in the way everlasting.

Have you taken a step back and asked the Lord to examine you? Try you, search you, see if there is any wicked way in you?

note.label: Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: David is describing the Lord and His ability to see and know all things. From the very beginning he says the Lord knows his downsitting and his uprising.
Whether he ascends up into heaven or makes his bed in hell, the Lord is there. There is nowhere a man can flee from His presence.
The darkness and the night are the same thing to the Lord. When the sun is out you see everything clearly, and the Lord says He sees the same thing even in the dark.
His reins are his life, his soul. When he says the Lord has possessed his reins, he means his life, and that the Lord covered him in his mother's womb.
The Lord's knowledge of David reaches back to when his substance was made in secret, before any of his members existed. The Lord is aware of all things at all times.
A key point David speaks about all the time is the Lord delivering him from his enemies and those that seek to hurt him.
Modern Christianity forgives and loves all things, but David says he hates them with a perfect hatred. He hates those that hate God, and that is the way the Lord wants His people to roll.
This does not mean you go out doing something crazy, but David does not care for those that do not care for the Lord. He counts them his enemies.
At the end he asks the Lord to search him, know his heart, try him, and see if there be any wicked way in him and lead him in the way everlasting.
